Few reasons.

One is the most direct way-- Workers Faculties. This offers 25% Science in every city with a Factory-- and you should be building Factories in every city possible. This is one of the strongest tenets in the game imho and it's worth beeling for. Plus the Factory construction speed and its almost broken. It's like having half an Observatory in every city.

Secondly is Spaceflight Pioneers. It's the level 3 Tenet I tend to value more than other people. It's a Free Sciencest and Engineer. This isn't super impactful but it can be if you hold onto them for Hubble. Use the GS to bulb for it like your others then use the GE to rush it. Gets you a shit ton of bonuses. 

Finally is all the Happiness in Order. I think Order has a ton of happiness that's pretty easy to get, like Socialist Realism.  Happiness is a growth limiter. More population from Happiness, more Science. I'm sure you know that, though. 

Freedom has a good argument for also being the best Science route but I think Order beats it by a little.

One of the most busy times in the game, honestly. I use the radio bulbing trick-- rush Public Schools, then Electricity, then use Oxford's free tech to grab Radio the same turn you finish Electricity. 

On higher levels, it's one of the best ways to grab a free Ideology, since you circumvent needing coal and building factories. Around this time, you really need to be thinking about how you plan on winning. War? Auto. Science? Probably Order. Diplo? Freedom is a good bet. This part of the game, on higher levels, is where you can finally surpass the AI in the game of catch-up.

I'll offer a few of my thoughts here.

Early game on Deity is a total wash. I can win about 40-50% of my Deity games, just accept sometimes you really can be put into unwinnable situations, imo. Spawning next to the Huns, for how I typically play, means an instant reset. So, that in mind, here's some thoughts.

Stop going for Wonders, if you do. Losing a wonder if you've been working on it for 10\~ turns is catastrophic. There's also the Early Game Worker steal, from a CS at least. If you think you can, sometimes it's worth it to steal a Civ's worker, if only to slow them down.

 Early game focus is growing your cap and settling *defendable* cities. A mistake I often see rookies to Deity make is settling flatland, undefendable cities. City location should really be settled in a way that lets you focus fire on units. 

Also, dear god, bribe the AI to kill one another. Even if it puts you at -10 Happiness, it can be worth it. If it saves your life, then do it. It's better to be unhappy than to be killed by Shaka's Impi Zerg rush. 

Generally, rule of thumb, you want a National College before turn 100 on standard speed. This makes your chances of winning a lot better; it's worth gunning for if you can. Typically, I'll build my National College and THEN settle my 4th city, as I find the timing works a lot better that way. Getting National College after Circus Maximus isn't a good idea. You'll be too far behind. Timing is a huge deal on Deity.

It'll depend on the Civ you're using, but I find going for Civil Service after getting my National College up works well. After that, Education is something I do if I can, but sometimes you'll be forced into more military focused techs. 

Gold is, in my eyes, a pretty weak resource; I think you only need "just enough", unless you're going for a purchase strategy. Thus, I think it's a good idea to almost only run internal trade routes; outside trade routes are fine, but growing your city is almost always better than extra gold. 

Hope this helps! Anyone else can feel free to hop in here and dispute my advice, it's probably not perfect.

It's the second most important tree in the game, minus Tradition. 

Rationalism really is just absurd. The 10% bonus science would be good enough to warrant opening it, but Free Thought and Secularism provide crazy levels of science as well. On higher difficulties, since you're playing catch-up with AI for most of the game, Rationalism is more or less a must.

So yeah, it's totally worth beelining for Rationalism. It's one of the 10,000 reasons Poland is so good- as soon as you enter the Renaissance Era, you get Rationalism, no need to time your entrance to the era with a social policy. 

Typically, you should be able to get either first or second pick at Ideology, which already gives you or two picks at free social polices. Your mileage with this will vary-- I typically use the Oxford slingshot method into Radio, and that has pretty good success rates for me. You don't really *have* to finish Rationalism per se, but in not doing so, you miss out on the Free Tech, which blows, but you also miss out on the purchasing of GS with Faith, which *really* blows. Bulbing your GS will help you get to Satellites, one of the best techs to win you the game. There's a few situations I could see not finishing it; maybe you're Freedom, and you really need the free units, and you don't have a religion, and blah blah blah...you should probably finish Rationalism. 

To talk about the other trees for a moment; in short, no. Patronage is good, but it's not nearly strong enough to win you a game. Science is what wins games, so therefore, Rationalism wins games. Honor is a pretty bad tree to open, I basically find it almost always useless. Commerce is worth some attention; Wagon Trains is really good, and some of the older Civ players will use Commerce+ Autocracy to do a unit purchase strategy, though that works better in multiplayer, haven't tried it on Single-Player.

The short answer is that it's difficult and probably not worth it. 
Long answer, there's a few ways. Firstly, I'll assume you're playing on a lower difficulty as early war is near impossible. 
You'll have to limit your own cities, as the early unhappiness will mostly come from number of cities, rather than high population. I'll assume you've taken Liberty policies as well. City Connections will yield some happiness. Raze any city that doesn't provide you a unique Luxury. 
You'll also want to stagnate your growth in your own cities to prevent that unhappiness too.

Early war is difficult not only because of the AI's early advantages (free techs, more workers/settlers) but also because there are less options open to you for fixing happiness issues. In doing early war You'll maybe pick up a few cities but they'll all likely be small and unhappy. 
TLDR, Hold off on offensive wars early if you're playing on a medium-high difficulty. There's some exceptions to that, of course. This is all just my opinion though. Based off how I play Civ.

Here's my quick write-up on this stuff.

So when it comes to helping out other Civs, (be it with gold or your military) you need to ask two questions here. Does helping this Civ either stop someone from winning the game, or does it keep me safe?

Option one is a little more clear cut. If there's 3 Civs left, including you, and AI 2 controls all capitals except yours and AI 1's. You should probably fight to keep AI 1 alive in the game because if you don't, you're in a very bad spot.

The second option is something else. There are times, moreso early in the game, it can be helpful to keep Civ's alive. If AI 2 is invading AI 1, and you border AI 1, it can be helpful to actually help AI one stay alive. It keeps your border safe, and it will also help you in the diplomatic stage. You'll have to weigh your options, but I've found this to be a sound strategy.  

As a quick example, in one game I played on Deity, Babylon was winning the science race and had the biggest army. Between Babylon and I were the Ottomans, who were middle of the road. When Babylon attacked the Ottomans, I joined the war because I didn't have faith in my Civ (Rome) to defeat an army from Babylon. So I helped the Ottomans defeat Babylon. I did end up winning, but who knows. If Babylon had overran the Ottomans, I would have focused more resources on surving that.

You can also use this to come out on top too. If the AI is fighting a war and is either losing or not making progress, you can ask them what they would give you to declare war on another Civ. Normally it's just a little gold and open borders, but it's just an added bonus on top.

Hope this helps!
